title: Bits
statementMd:
Let's denote as ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/6500127ba81ee2a9ffdacf23b301df518aa9cd65.png) the number of bits set ('1' bits) in the binary representation of the non-negative integer $*x*$.

You are given multiple queries consisting of pairs of integers $*l*$ and $*r*$. For each query, find the $*x*$, such that $*l* ≤ *x* ≤ *r*$, and ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/6500127ba81ee2a9ffdacf23b301df518aa9cd65.png) is maximum possible. If there are multiple such numbers find the smallest of them.

## Input

The first line contains integer $*n*$ — the number of queries ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 10000$).

Each of the following $*n*$ lines contain two integers $*l*_{*i*}, *r*_{*i*}$ — the arguments for the corresponding query ($0 ≤ *l*_{*i*} ≤ *r*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{18}$).

## Output

For each query print the answer in a separate line.

## Note

The binary representations of numbers from 1 to 10 are listed below:

$1_{10} = 1_{2}$

$2_{10} = 10_{2}$

$3_{10} = 11_{2}$

$4_{10} = 100_{2}$

$5_{10} = 101_{2}$

$6_{10} = 110_{2}$

$7_{10} = 111_{2}$

$8_{10} = 1000_{2}$

$9_{10} = 1001_{2}$

$10_{10} = 1010_{2}$
